subject: Coordinating a short demo across US customer + EU team — proposed windows

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Ellie Park <ellie.park@midwesthealth.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 14:12:00 -0400
Subject: Quick demo — finding the overlap (US customer + EU host)

Hi Jordan / Ellie,

Thanks again for your interest in Redwood Inference. We’d love to run a 30-minute walkthrough focused on latency/cost controls and a short Q&A. I want to avoid the usual timezone ping-pong, so below are realistic options taking DST and regional hours into account:

Option A — EU-hosted window (single call):
- Tue Nov 2, 17:30–18:00 CET (08:30–09:00 PT / 11:30–12:00 ET) — EU team can fully host, good for live kernel-level Q&A.

Option B — US-friendly early window (EU joins late):
- Wed Nov 3, 08:00–08:30 PT (17:00–17:30 CET) — EU hosts may be on a later-than-normal hour but can rotate.

Option C — Split-hand off (short synchronous + follow-up):
- 20-minute EU-led walkthrough at 17:00 CET + 10-minute US PM follow-up the next morning local to you. This reduces late-evening burden for EU team and keeps customer-facing time earlier for you.

Notes:
- DST: US switches Nov 1 this year; EU switches earlier in Oct, so offsets change that week. I’ve attached an .ics with our team availability per local time and a small deck.
- If you have an APAC stakeholder, we can record the main portion and do a separate 15-min handoff at their morning local time.

Please let me know which slot you prefer (A/B/C) and who will be the primary technical attendee from your side. I’ll send a Google Calendar invite with timezones explicitly displayed once we lock it.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
